この・その・あの・どの + Noun
ここ・そこ・あそこ・どこ

title: This, that, that over there
canDo: I can point at something near me, near the listener or far from both of us, and ask what it is (これは / それは / あれは なんですか).
I can say "this dictionary" or "that person" with この / その / あの + noun, and ask "which one?" with どれ and どの.
I can ask where a place is (〜は どこですか) and understand ここ / そこ / あそこ in the answer.
I can ask whose something is (だれの) and answer "it's mine", "it's Maria's".

blocks.t: Warm-up: pick up 3 objects at home and say the name of each one in Japanese
Vocabulary: tap 🔊 on each word and repeat it twice
Grammar: the 4 points, pointing at real objects while you read the examples, and one 🔬 per point
Lesson 2 video (block 6), pausing on the examples
Notebook homework + checking it against the answer key
Checklist (block 10) + write your questions in the lesson notebook

skills: Building X は Y です and questions with か and with なんですか (lesson 01-1).
Linking two nouns with の: わたしの なまえ (lesson 01-1).
Reading basic katakana for names (マリア, ルーカス); the kana is always written out.

vocab.en: that over there (far from both of us)
over there (far from both of us)

grammar.title: これ・それ・あれ・どれ
grammar.gloss: this, that, that over there, which one
grammar.explanation:
These four words **point at things** and stand **on their own**, in place of a noun. So they fill the same slots as any noun: they can be the TOPIC (これは…) or the PREDICATE (…あれです).
• **これ**: near **the speaker** (in my hand, right in front of me).
• **それ**: near **the listener** (in the other person's hand, next to them).
• **あれ**: **far from both** (across the street, at the back of the room).
• **どれ**: "which one?", to choose among three or more things. (For choosing between two, there is another word, in lesson 10-1.)
Japanese decides by **distance from the people talking**. English has only "this" and "that", so English "that" is split in two: それ if the thing is near the listener, あれ if it is far from both of you.
grammar.structure: これ / それ / あれ は [N] です。 · [N] は どれですか。

examples.jp: これは わたしの さいふです。
examples.kana: これは わたしの さいふです。
examples.romaji: Kore wa watashi no saifu desu.

examples.jp: それは なんですか。— じしょです。
examples.kana: それは なんですか。— じしょです。
examples.romaji: Sore wa nan desu ka. — Jisho desu.
examples.en: What's that (near you)? — It's a dictionary.

examples.jp: マリアさんの かばんは どれですか。— あれです。
examples.kana: マリアさんの かばんは どれですか。— あれです。
examples.romaji: Maria-san no kaban wa dore desu ka. — Are desu.
examples.en: Which one is Maria's bag? — That one over there. [lit. as for Maria's bag, which one is it?]

pitfalls: これ doesn't go before a noun: "this book" is この ほん (point 4b). これ ほん ✗ → この ほん ✓.
A question word doesn't take は: どれは ✗. The thing you're looking for takes は, and どれ goes where the answer goes: 〜は どれですか ✓.
The point of view flips in the answer. If someone points at what's in YOUR hand and asks それは なんですか, answer これは… ✓, not それは… ✗.
Don't translate English "that" with それ every time. Think about where the thing is: with me → これ; with you → それ; far from both of us → あれ.
howToStudy: Put one object in your hand, another on a chair (playing the listener) and a third across the room. Point at each one and say out loud これは…, それは…, あれは….
Tap 🔬 on example 3: マリアさんの shows up as DESCRIBES NEXT (it describes かばん), かばんは is the TOPIC and どれですか is the PREDICATE. The answer あれです takes the same place as どれですか.
In your notebook, write 3 sentences with これ, それ and あれ about things in your home.

grammar.title: この・その・あの・どの + N
grammar.gloss: this ~, that ~, that ~ over there, which ~
grammar.explanation:
The same family of distances, but now the word is **attached to a noun** and describes it: この ほん = "this book". この never stands alone: it always needs a noun after it.
• この: near the speaker · その: near the listener · あの: far from both · どの: "which ~?".
• The block この ほん works as **a single noun**: it can be the TOPIC (この ほんは…) or the PREDICATE (…この ほんです).
• Tip: the **-re** forms (これ) stand alone; the **-no** forms (この) need a noun after them, like the の from lesson 01-1.
• あの ひと ("that person") is the normal way to talk about someone over there.
grammar.structure: この / その / あの [N] は 〜です。 · どの [N] ですか。

examples.jp: この じしょは にほんごの じしょです。
examples.kana: この じしょは にほんごの じしょです。
examples.romaji: Kono jisho wa nihongo no jisho desu.
examples.en: This dictionary is a Japanese dictionary.

examples.jp: あの ひとは りゅうがくせいです。
examples.kana: あの ひとは りゅうがくせいです。
examples.en: That person over there is an international student.

examples.jp: どの かさですか。— その かさです。
examples.kana: どの かさですか。— その かさです。
examples.romaji: Dono kasa desu ka. — Sono kasa desu.
examples.en: Which umbrella is it? — That umbrella (near you).

pitfalls: この never stands alone: この です ✗ → これです ✓ or この かさです ✓.
Don't mix up あの ("that ~ over there") and あのう ("um…", for hesitating or getting someone's attention): あの ひと = "that person"; あのう、すみません = "um, excuse me".
"This book" is この ほん: これの ほん ✗ → この ほん ✓.
For people, don't use これ / それ / あれ: "who is that?" is あの ひとは だれですか ✓, not あれは だれですか ✗, which treats the person like a thing and can sound rude.
howToStudy: Swap the words from point 4a for この/その/あの + noun, out loud: これ → この さいふ; それ → その とけい; あれ → あの じてんしゃ.
Tap 🔬 on example 1: この shows up as DESCRIBES NEXT, attached to じしょは (the TOPIC), and にほんごの is also DESCRIBES NEXT, attached to じしょです (the PREDICATE).
Look out the window and ask 3 questions with あの: あの ひとは せんせいですか。, あの じてんしゃは….

grammar.title: ここ・そこ・あそこ・どこ
grammar.explanation:
The same family, now for **places**: **ここ** (here, where I am), **そこ** (there, near you), **あそこ** (over there, far from both of us), **どこ** (where?). To ask where something is, the place you're looking for is the TOPIC and どこ goes in the PREDICATE: ゆうびんきょくは どこですか。 The answer swaps どこ for the information: ゆうびんきょくは あそこです。
• Notice the form: the pattern breaks here, and it's あそこ, not "あこ".
• ここ can also be the topic: ここは としょかんです ("this place is the library", said while you're in it).
• Just like English "is" in "the post office is over there", です here tells where something is: X は あそこです. (The verbs for "there is / exists" come in lesson 04-1.)
• With a school or a company, 〜は どこですか can also ask **which one**: ルーカスさんの だいがくは どこですか。— サンパウロだいがくです。 Both kinds of answer (the city or the name) are fine.
grammar.structure: [place/thing] は どこですか。— ここ / そこ / あそこ です。 · ここは [place] です。

examples.jp: すみません、ゆうびんきょくは どこですか。— あそこです。
examples.kana: すみません、ゆうびんきょくは どこですか。— あそこです。
examples.romaji: Sumimasen, yūbinkyoku wa doko desu ka. — Asoko desu.
examples.en: Excuse me, where is the post office? — It's over there.

examples.jp: ここは だいがくの としょかんです。
examples.kana: ここは だいがくの としょかんです。
examples.romaji: Koko wa daigaku no toshokan desu.
examples.en: This is the university library. [lit. as for here, the university's library is]

examples.jp: ルーカスさんの だいがくは どこですか。— サンパウロです。
examples.kana: ルーカスさんの だいがくは どこですか。— サンパウロです。
examples.romaji: Rūkasu-san no daigaku wa doko desu ka. — Sanpauro desu.
examples.en: Where is Lucas's university? — It's in São Paulo.

pitfalls: ここ is a place and これ is a thing: ここは なんですか asks "what is this place?"; これは なんですか asks "what is this?".
どこ is never the topic: どこは ✗. The place you're looking for takes は, and どこ goes at the end: きっさてんは どこですか ✓.
English "there" is two words in Japanese: そこ (near the listener) and あそこ (far from both of you). Pointing at a building across the street: そこです ✗ → あそこです ✓.
howToStudy: Imagine you're on campus and act out the dialogue out loud, changing the place 4 times: としょかんは どこですか。— あそこです。 (ゆうびんきょく, きっさてん…)
Tap 🔬 on example 1: すみません is an INTERJECTION, ゆうびんきょくは is the TOPIC and どこですか is the PREDICATE. In the answer, only the predicate changes.
Draw a small map in your notebook with 4 places and write a question and an answer for each one.

grammar.title: だれの N
grammar.explanation:
だれ = "who". With the の from lesson 01-1, **だれの** becomes "whose": だれの かばん = "whose bag". As always, the question word goes where the answer goes: それは **だれの** かばんですか。— **マリアさんの** かばんです。
• When the noun is obvious, it can disappear and の stays on its own: マリアさんのです ("it's Maria's"), わたしのです ("it's mine"). This の works like English "'s" or "mine": it stands for "the one belonging to…".
• The question can be short too: その かさは だれのですか。
• With older people or in formal situations, you'll hear **どなた**, the more polite form of だれ.
grammar.structure: [thing] は だれの [N] ですか。— [person] の ([N]) です。

examples.jp: それは だれの じしょですか。— すずきさんの じしょです。
examples.kana: それは だれの じしょですか。— すずきさんの じしょです。
examples.romaji: Sore wa dare no jisho desu ka. — Suzuki-san no jisho desu.
examples.en: Whose dictionary is that? — It's Mr./Ms. Suzuki's dictionary.

examples.jp: あの じてんしゃは だれのですか。— ルーカスさんのです。
examples.kana: あの じてんしゃは だれのですか。— ルーカスさんのです。
examples.romaji: Ano jitensha wa dare no desu ka. — Rūkasu-san no desu.
examples.en: Whose is that bicycle over there? — It's Lucas's.

examples.jp: この とけいは わたしのです。
examples.kana: この とけいは わたしのです。
examples.romaji: Kono tokei wa watashi no desu.

pitfalls: Don't forget の in the answer: ルーカスさんです ✗ would say the bicycle "is Lucas" → ルーカスさんのです ✓.
だれですか asks "who is it?" (a person). だれのですか asks "whose is it?" (a thing).
"Mine" is わたしの: この とけいは わたしです ✗ means "this watch is me" → この とけいは わたしのです ✓.
howToStudy: Pick up 4 objects at home and ask out loud, with the right distance word: これは だれの 〜ですか。 Answer yourself: 〜さんのです / わたしのです.
Tap 🔬 on example 2: だれのですか and ルーカスさんのです both show up as the PREDICATE — the answer takes exactly the question word's place.
In your notebook, write 3 question-and-answer pairs with だれの, one of them without the noun in the answer.

homework.intro: Do it by hand in your notebook, writing the Japanese in kana. For the situations, draw one stick figure for the speaker and another for the listener if it helps. Only then open the answer key, item by item. Circle what you got wrong and redo it the next day.

tasks.prompt: Choose これ, それ or あれ by distance and write the sentence.

items.q: The dictionary is in your hand. Say: "This is my dictionary."

a.jp: これは わたしの じしょです。
a.romaji: Kore wa watashi no jisho desu.

items.q: Ana is holding a bag. Ask her if it's hers.

a.jp: それは アナさんの かばんですか。
a.romaji: Sore wa Ana-san no kaban desu ka.

items.note: Near the listener: それ. "Hers" = アナさんの: use her name, not "you".

items.q: There's a bicycle across the street. Ask whose it is.

a.jp: あれは だれの じてんしゃですか。
a.romaji: Are wa dare no jitensha desu ka.

items.q: You're holding an umbrella and someone asks それは なんですか。 Answer: "This is an umbrella."
items.note: It's in your hand: これ, even though the question used それ.

tasks.prompt: Fill in the right word: この/その/あの/どの (with a noun after it) or これ/それ/あれ/どれ (on their own).

items.q: ＿ かばんは わたしのです。 (the bag is in your own hand: near the speaker)
＿は なんですか。 (the thing is near the listener)
items.note: On its own, before は: the -re form.

items.q: ＿ ひとは せんせいですか。 (the person is far from both of you)
マリアさんの かさは ＿ですか。 ("which one?")
＿ じしょですか。— その じしょです。 ("which dictionary?")
Where is the library? — It's over there.

a.jp: としょかんは どこですか。— あそこです。
a.romaji: Toshokan wa doko desu ka. — Asoko desu.

items.q: (You're standing inside it.) This place is a coffee shop.

a.jp: ここは きっさてんです。

items.note: A place you're in: ここ, not これ.

items.q: Whose watch is this? — It's Maria's.

a.jp: この とけいは だれのですか。— マリアさんのです。
a.romaji: Kono tokei wa dare no desu ka. — Maria-san no desu.

items.note: これは だれの とけいですか。 is also correct.

items.q: That person over there is Professor Tanaka.

a.jp: あの ひとは たなかせんせいです。

items.note: せんせい can follow a name instead of さん.

items.q: Where is the post office? — It's there (near you).

a.jp: ゆうびんきょくは どこですか。— そこです。
a.romaji: Yūbinkyoku wa doko desu ka. — Soko desu.

a.jp: この さいふは わたしのです。
a.romaji: Kono saifu wa watashi no desu.

tasks.prompt: Look around the place where you are and write 4 sentences: one with これ, one with あの + noun, one with ここは and one question with だれの. Then read them aloud, pointing.

items.q: Model (match its structure, not its words):

a.jp: これは わたしの とけいです。あの じてんしゃは ペドロさんのです。ここは わたしの だいがくです。その かばんは だれのですか。
a.romaji: Kore wa watashi no tokei desu. Ano jitensha wa Pedoro-san no desu. Koko wa watashi no daigaku desu. Sono kaban wa dare no desu ka.
a.en: This is my watch. That bicycle over there is Pedro's. This place is my university. Whose is that bag (near you)?

items.note: Check: これ and ここ on their own, この/その/あの always with a noun, and の after the owner (ペドロさんの) when the noun is left out.

practice.what: Play normally and hunt for これ, それ, あれ, この, その, あの, ここ, そこ, あそこ and どこ in the dialogues. Each time, pause and ask yourself: who is the thing or place near? Copy 2 of those lines into your notebook.
Lesson 2 vocabulary in the SRS. Then Drills → 🔬 Anatomy → 🧱 Build from the end: 5 sentences.
Practice L2: do the comprehension part, paying attention to who is near what.
Tap 🔊 on each example in this lesson and repeat along 3 times, pointing at a real object as you speak.
House tour: walk through the rooms for 3 minutes saying ここは…, これは…, あれは… out loud, plus one question with だれの. Record it and listen back.

culture.title: Exchanging business cards
culture.body: In Japanese working life, introductions usually come with an exchange of **business cards**, めいし. You hand your card over with **both hands**, turned so the other person can read your name, while saying はじめまして。…よろしく おねがいします。 The person receiving it also uses both hands, reads the card carefully and, in a meeting, usually leaves it on the table in front of them until the end of the conversation. Putting the card straight into a trouser pocket, or writing on it in front of the person, is usually seen as careless. When both people hand over their cards at the same time, the more junior person often holds theirs slightly lower than the other person's.
culture.try: Write your name in katakana on a card-sized piece of paper. Practice handing it over with both hands, text facing the other person, saying: はじめまして。(your name)です。よろしく おねがいします。 Then practice receiving: take it with both hands and read the name aloud.

checklist: I choose これ, それ or あれ by the right distance, without thinking of English "this/that".
I use この/その/あの always with a noun after them, and これ/それ/あれ always on their own.
I can ask where a place is (〜は どこですか) and answer with ここ, そこ or あそこ.
I can ask whose something is (だれの) and answer 〜のです without forgetting the の.
I know that question words (どれ, どこ) don't take は.
I did the homework, checked it against the answer key and redid what I got wrong.
